During the high-temperature creep process, the needle-like brittle TCP phase precipitates along the [110] orientation on the {111} crystal plane in the dendritic stem region

attributes.morphology: N-type rafting perpendicular to stress; labyrinth pattern; topological inversion to elliptical irregular structure

evidence.section: 3.1 Evolution of TCP phase during creep
evidence.quote: Rafting perpendicular to the direction of the stress (N-type raft) occurred ... the γ/γ' microstructure exhibited a 'maze' pattern ... approximately elliptical irregular structure.

evidence.section: 3.2 Effects of TCP phase on creep properties
evidence.quote: The γ/γ' two-phase microstructure near the micro-cracks appears as a 'wave-like' structure, and a topological inversion phenomenon can be observed.

attributes.morphology: zigzag propagation path, perpendicular to stress direction

evidence.section: 3.2 Effects of TCP phase on creep properties
evidence.quote: A number of micro-cracks perpendicular to the direction of the stress can be distinctly observed. These micro-cracks often nucleate from the internal inclusions or microstructure defects ... a crack that extends with a roughly zigzag shape.
The precipitation of the TCP phase causes the consumption of the main solid solution strengthening elements Re and W in the γ phase, weakens the solid solution strengthening effect of the two phases
The TCP phase is rich in matrix phase forming elements, which weakens the solid solution strengthening effect and causes the dissolution of adjacent matrix phases.
dislocations have difficulty climbing or cutting the TCP phase so they accumulate at the TCP/γ' phase interface, causing stress concentration in the vicinity as well as crack initiation
the creep crack nucleates from the TCP phase, and after the crack nucleates, its propagation path coincides with the growth direction of the TCP phase
